summary: Iteration 3 VISUAL overhaul verification: All 5 biomes (dungeon/hell/sakura/ice/tech) successfully load with new 640x448 canvas and clearly differentiated tilemap aesthetics. Confirmed: (1) Canvas at 640x448 (data-testid=game-canvas) for all biomes. (2) Stone-brick floor with mortar seams + crack variations clearly visible in dungeon. (3) 3D wall shading present (lighter top row, darker bottom shadow band) across all biomes. (4) HELL biome: obsidian dark-red/black floor with bright orange lava strips, deep red brick walls with glowing cracks - excellent visual differentiation. (5) SAKURA biome: warm tan wood-plank floor with grain + pink petal speckles, green bamboo wall accents - clear differentiation. (6) ICE biome: light-blue ice block floor (lighter/darker alternation), pale-blue brick walls with shine. (7) TECH biome: dark navy metal panels with cyan circuit traces + LED dots, deep blue walls with neon seams. (8) Wall-mounted torches visible on top + bottom walls of every room with glowing halos (biome-tinted: orange in dungeon/hell, pink in sakura, cyan in ice/tech). (9) Chests spawn in corners (e.g., top-left and bottom-right) confirmed in every biome. (10) Robots are drawn ON a visible colored rug/platform (orange for hell, pink for sakura, light-cyan for ice, dark-cyan for tech, magenta/gold for dungeon). (11) Mini-map at top-right has metallic frame with bolts at all 4 corners, gradient grey border - looks polished. (12) Entities (player ~26px, robot ~32px, mobs) are visibly larger than iteration_2 (was 22px), no longer tiny squares. (13) HUD still shows 'BIOME · ROOM 1 / 6' correctly. (14) 0 console errors / 0 page errors switching between all 5 biomes.

issues: Mini-map biome label like 'DUNGEON 1/6' still appears slightly clipped at the top edge of the metallic frame (the text overlaps the top frame border in all 5 biomes). Carry-over from iter2 - the new metallic frame did not push the label down. Recommend rendering the label INSIDE the frame body (below the top metallic band) or shifting the entire mini-map block down by ~10px so the label has clearance.

Dungeon stone-brick is good but the crack variations are very faint (1px marks). Compared to hell/sakura/ice/tech which all have strong biome-specific accents (lava strips, petals, circuit traces), the dungeon floor reads slightly flatter. Suggest stronger crack patterns or occasional rune/mossy variant tiles in dungeon to match the visual richness of other biomes.

Tech-biome torches still use the same wooden bracket as fantasy biomes. For a sci-fi consistent feel consider a thin metal sconce / glowing strip lamp in tech biome (and ice biome). Minor polish item.

action_items: (Cosmetic) Move mini-map biome label down so it sits inside the metallic frame instead of clipping against the top bolt row. Either render the label below the top frame band (y offset ~ MM_Y + 4) or push the entire MM block down to leave clearance.
(Polish) Strengthen dungeon-biome floor cracks/runes so dungeon floor reads as rich as the hell/sakura/ice/tech variants - currently dungeon looks the plainest.
(Polish) Consider biome-appropriate torch brackets for tech (metal strip lamp) and ice (icicle sconce) biomes; the rest are good.
(From iter2, unresolved) Robot Good-Job double-lock still cannot be deeply verified in automation due to skeleton-lethality near robots; code path is intact.
critical_code_review_comments: sprites.js drawTorch / drawRug / drawMiniMapFrame are clean and parameterised by biome - good separation.
ProbabilityDungeon.jsx render order is correct: floor -> pits -> rugs -> walls -> torches -> chests -> robots -> mobs -> player. Rugs correctly drawn BEFORE walls/robots (matches spec).
Canvas size constants COLS=20 ROWS=14 TILE=32 -> 640x448 match the spec exactly and HUD reflects it.
ROOM_CHESTS arrays place chests at corners (e.g., x=TILE near walls), verified visually in all biomes.
ProbabilityDungeon.jsx is still ~700+ lines (carry-over). Splitting render / room-build / loop into separate modules would help maintainability.
Mini-map label rendering: see action item - the y position of the label text needs +6-8px offset so it doesn't sit on the metallic frame top band.

drawFloorTile - the dungeon variant cracked pattern uses (variant*13)%7==0 which yields ~14% of tiles; cracks themselves are only 3 tiny 1px rects - low visual impact. Consider thicker/more visible cracks.

success_rate.frontend: ~98% (all 13 declared visual checkpoints PASS; only cosmetic mini-map label clipping + minor polish suggestions remain)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use [data-testid=hub-dungeon-btn] (NOT 'PLAY') to start the dungeon from MainHub. BiomeSelect screen appears only when entering from hub if multiple biomes unlocked - directly setting currentBiome in localStorage skips the select screen and lands you in the playing canvas. Canvas is now 640x448 (data-testid=game-canvas). For each biome, screenshot the canvas region (clip bounding box +15px padding) to see the metallic mini-map frame too. All visual checkpoints from review_request features are confirmed PASS - only cosmetic polish items remain.
rca of the issue: N/A - no functional bugs found. Mini-map label clip is a cosmetic carry-over from iteration_2: the new drawMiniMapFrame renders a metallic top band at y=MM_Y-4..MM_Y, but the biome label text is drawn at approximately y=MM_Y+8 which overlaps the frame's top inner edge. Fix: render label at y=MM_Y+12 or shift MM_Y down by 8px so the label has visual clearance.
